threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by their confusion over the 'weird' bus routes that seem to loop back on themselves; only locals know that's just how it goes here.
Last night, a group of teens on the 133 were debating the best chicken shops, while a guy in the corner kept trying to film them. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stepped outside and the waft of grilled kebabs mingled with the chatter of kids playing in the street. That’s Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a karaoke bar where locals earnestly belt out German punk hits at 2 AM, surrounded by friendly strangers. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by the way they know to bypass the Civic Center when there's a dog on the tracks. Tourists just stand there confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a bus driver did a whole karaoke set while we sat idling. Definitely a Muni moment—only in SF do you get a show with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can haggle at local markets like Els Encants. Vendors here see that as an affront; it’s about respect, not just price.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to try the local ‘patates braves’—still preferring the bland chain fare close to their Airbnb.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: If you still call it Dalston Junction instead of just 'the Junction', you definitely haven't settled in yet.
Caught a bloke serenading the driver on the 59 last night, proper crooning. Made the journey to Streatham feel like a mini concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy in a full suit rummaging through a dumpster for a vintage record – only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find döner kebab shops open at 3 AM, serving fresh food to soothe late-night revelers right off the dance floor.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local would know that the smell of burnt toast lingers around Dolores Park when the fog rolls in. It hits different.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the 5-Fulton today, trying to pass the time. Just another day on Muni, where the unexpected is the norm.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Festa Major' is just a party, but it’s a month-long affair where locals bring their best carry dishes to share. It’s deep-rooted tradition.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newcomers by the way they take pictures of the metro maps. The locals just know where they’re going.
